issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to have an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12), and the Bookstore class declares its books property as an array ([Book]). However, the solution implements the initializer as init(books: Set<Book>) which conflicts with the specified array type and with the Client code that calls Bookstore(books: books) passing an [Book]. This constructor parameter type mismatch will prevent the code from compiling and confuses students about the correct initializer signature they are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer accept an array of Book as specified: change the initializer signature to init(books: [Book]) and assign self.books = books. This aligns the initializer with the books property type and with the Client code that passes an [Book].

issues.description: The problem statement requires an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (an array) for the Bookstore, but the solution's Bookstore implements init(books: Set<Book>) (a Set). This mismatch between the expected initializer signature and the solution's initializer creates a mapping/confusion for students: the assembleBookstore helper in the solution builds an [Book] and calls Bookstore(books: books), which does not match the solution initializer type, and the problem text explicitly documents the array-based signature. Students will be unsure which constructor signature to implement and may face compile-time/type errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer consistent with the problem statement and the rest of the code by changing the solution initializer to init(books: [Book]) (use an array), or alternatively update the problem statement (and all references) to require init(books: Set<Book>) if a Set is intended. Prefer changing the solution to init(books: [Book]) to match the documented requirement and the assembleBookstore usage.
